findings.title: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no argument, which matches no declaration, so the services module fails to compile
findings.description: Line 47 reads `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`. The only declaration of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` in the repo is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`. A repo-wide search finds no zero-argument overload in `UsernameForm`, `UsernamePasswordForm`, or the other callers (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:115` and `:137`). javac will reject line 47, so `UsernameForm` and everything depending on the services module cannot build. The fix is to pass `context.getUser()`, which is already non-null at that point.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) returns false when user is null, so the username-first passkey conditional UI is never set up
findings.description:
The helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Its two call sites were converted from checks that fired when the user was null. Per the removed lines in the diff, the original `authenticate()` fill sat in the `else` branch of `if (context.getUser() != null)`, and the original `challenge(context, error, field)` checked `context.getUser() == null`. The call sites are now at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:115` and `:137`, and with no user both evaluate to false.

The path is: open the login page with no user, then `authenticate()` (line 115) is false, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm` never runs. `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` is never set, so `themes/.../passkeys.ftl:2` does not render `<form id="webauth">` or the conditional-UI script. `login.ftl` and `login-username.ftl` then emit `autocomplete="username"` instead of `"username webauthn"`. The username-not-found and error re-renders through line 137 lose the same setup. `OrganizationAuthenticator.java:357-361` has its own no-user fill, so the regression is limited to the `UsernamePasswordForm`/`UsernameForm` path.

The new fill for the re-authentication case is correct and should stay. The no-user fill must also keep running. Dropping the `user != null` term from the helper would fix both cases. The existing assertions at `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:142-146` and `:191-196` check the conditional-UI autocomplete and the `webauth` form on the initial no-user page, so they would fail as written.
